group_assessment.weighting: The observations are weighted HIGH and the comparative design is the reason: the two drugs were run head-to-head in the same patient-derived lines with the same endpoints, so the amlexanox negative is internally controlled rather than inferred across studies. The interpretation is weighted MEDIUM-LOW and in one specific direction: this group's standing programme is ataluren (its references 14 and 22, Shwachman-Diamond syndrome), which is a declared directional interest in favour of the comparator. That is a reason to read the amlexanox arm as the one they had least incentive to make work, and also a reason not to take the ataluren arm at face value. The amlexanox arms are also the smallest in the paper (n = 3 on the genotoxicity endpoints).
group_assessment.verdict: Verona Cystic Fibrosis Centre (V. Bezzerri, senior) with Gaslini haematology (Genoa), Insubria genomics and CNR-IRGB. Independent of the Lille group that originated the amlexanox claim: no shared author, no shared institution. Cell models from two public biobanks (Telethon Network Genetic Biobanks / Gaslini; NIGMS Coriell GM16757).

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: JATS body present and parsed; four body sections plus eight figure captions and two supplementary-material containers enumerated from the artefact.

entries.proposition: Amlexanox did NOTHING in one of the two nonsense-mutated genes tested, in patient-derived cells.
entries.snippet: On the contrary, we observed no effect on FANCF protein levels following amlexanox treatment in these cells (Fig. 1B).
entries.anchor: Results, first subsection, after the FANCF baseline (~40% of healthy control) and the FANCA baseline (just under 5%).

entries.proposition: In the other gene it raised full-length protein to about 9% of healthy control, against about 11% for the comparator.
entries.snippet: In this case, both ataluren and amlexanox were able to significantly induce FANCA full-length protein synthesis to almost 11% and 9% of healthy controls, respectively (Fig. 1C).
entries.anchor: Results, first subsection, after the FANCF baseline (~40% of healthy control) and the FANCA baseline (just under 5%).

entries.proposition: The NMD-inhibition arm of the 2012 claim was tested here and did NOT reproduce: NMD was active in the cells and amlexanox did not restore the transcript.
entries.snippet: We observed that NMD is activated in these cells, resulting in a 3-fold reduction of FANCA mRNA. However, neither amlexanox nor ataluren was able to rescue FANCA transcription (Supplementary Fig. 1A, B).
entries.anchor: Results, first subsection, immediately after the FANCA protein result.

entries.proposition: THE RELEVANT NEGATIVE: the protein gain did not become a phenotype gain. Amlexanox failed on both functional endpoints while the comparator in the same cells succeeded.
entries.snippet: Conversely, amlexanox showed no effect on either MMC- or DEB-induced genotoxicity in FA-A cells (Fig. 4), despite a slight increase in FANCA protein synthesis and a significant reduction of initial p53 levels.
entries.anchor: Results, third subsection ('Ataluren, but not amlexanox, mitigates genotoxic damage...'), final sentence.

entries.proposition: The authors state the general lesson themselves, and it is the lesson the known-roads reconnaissance needs: an intermediate marker moving is not a phenotype rescued.
entries.snippet: Thus, this study suggests that a partial downregulation of p53 per se is not sufficient to produce phenotypic rescue in human cells.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph comparing the two drugs on the genotoxic endpoints.

entries.proposition: The measured effect of amlexanox in this system is attributed by its own authors to a mechanism that is NOT read-through — TBK1/IKK-epsilon inhibition read out as a fall in pSTAT2.
entries.snippet: In this model, amlexanox significantly reduced pSTAT2 levels (by almost 50%) after 24 h of incubation (Fig. 5C). Interestingly, treatment with NF-κB inhibitors resulted in similar pSTAT2 reduction, suggesting that the overall effect of amlexanox is mainly due to its inhibitory effects on the TBK1/IKKε pathway.
entries.anchor: Results, fourth subsection, after the IL-6 / TNF-alpha negative.

entries.proposition: The paper's own closing methodological demand is the gate this reconnaissance should put on the amlexanox road.
entries.snippet: These findings emphasize the need for a reliable experimental pipeline to assess whether the minimal amount of neomorphic protein synthesized upon translational read-through is actually followed by phenotypic rescue.

entries.proposition: Scope limit to carry with every number above: the amlexanox arms are the smallest in the paper, and the systems are haematopoietic and dermal, never neural.
entries.snippet: Mitomycin C test of FA-F (A) and FA-A (B) LCL, after 24 h incubation with amlexanox 25μM (n = 3).
entries.anchor: Figure 4 caption, first sentence (caption read from the artefact; the panels were NOT inspected as images).

entries.proposition: The 10%-suffices premise that makes 9% sound adequate is imported from another disease, by citation, and is not measured here.
entries.snippet: Nevertheless, it should be noted that experience from Cystic Fibrosis highly effective modulator therapies revealed that a restoration of 10% of functional protein should be sufficient to significantly rescue the phenotype in inherited recessive diseases [42].
entries.anchor: Discussion, second paragraph, immediately after the amlexanox 9% figure.
